verdicts.reason: A reads in the right order: eyebrow, then headline, body, CTA, with the book on the right and a confetti strip as a brand cue. Its logo, though, is a tiny illegible mark crammed beside the legal text at bottom-left. B puts the CTA pill at the very top above the book and headline, moves the eyebrow below the body copy and enlarges it to compete with the headline, drops the confetti, and shrinks the logo to an unreadable speck.

A opens with the fine-print legal line at the top and buries the eyebrow at the bottom. Its CTA is a tiny pill jammed in the bottom-right corner next to an illegible logo, so the hierarchy and reading order are broken. B's CTA wrongly leads at the top and its eyebrow sits below the body, but the CTA is at least visible and the headline is clear, so B is marginally less broken.

A has a sensible book-left, copy-right layout with a strong headline and a prominent CTA. However, the eyebrow is shrunk to tiny text below the body copy, the legal text wraps raggedly, and the logo is illegible and sits on the confetti. B leads with the CTA above everything, has an oversized eyebrow below the body, no confetti and a microscopic logo.

In A the headline leads, but the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill floating at the right edge and the legal text is a cramped column at the left. The book is jammed into the confetti strip at the bottom and the logo has disappeared. B wrongly puts the CTA first and has an oversized eyebrow below the body, but it keeps a legible CTA and a (tiny) logo.
